reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
clinicalPearls: Caused by deficiency of asparagine synthetase (ASNS), which synthesises asparagine from aspartate and glutamine, making asparagine conditionally essential for the developing brain
Presents with congenital or progressive microcephaly, severe developmental impairment, intractable seizures, and hyperekplexia-like exaggerated startle or spasticity
Because the blood-brain barrier restricts asparagine entry, brain tissue depends on local synthesis, so the defect causes a functional cerebral asparagine deficiency

The biochemical picture is subtle: plasma amino acids may be near-normal, and low or low-normal asparagine (sometimes with low glutamine or raised aspartate/glutamate) in plasma or CSF is a clue rather than a definitive marker
Diagnosis usually rests on molecular confirmation of ASNS mutations rather than a striking metabolite abnormality
There is no established effective therapy; dietary asparagine supplementation has uncertain benefit because brain uptake is limited, and care is largely supportive
Inheritance is autosomal recessive with a severe, often early-fatal course
British spelling and paediatric context apply
reference.pathophysiology: Asparagine synthetase catalyses the ATP-dependent transfer of an amino group from glutamine to aspartate, forming asparagine and glutamate. Neurons depend on endogenous synthesis because asparagine crosses the blood-brain barrier poorly, so loss of enzyme activity produces a functional asparagine deficiency in the central nervous system, and possibly local accumulation of aspartate and glutamate that may be excitotoxic. The resulting disturbance of protein synthesis and amino acid homeostasis in the developing brain causes impaired neuronal proliferation and connectivity, manifesting as congenital microcephaly, severe encephalopathy, and refractory seizures. The peripheral biochemical changes are often mild, reflecting the primarily central nature of the deficiency.
additionalDifferentials: Other genetic causes of congenital microcephaly with epileptic encephalopathy
Hyperekplexia from glycine-receptor or transporter mutations
additionalInvestigations: Plasma and CSF amino acids looking for low/low-normal asparagine and related changes
Brain MRI for microcephaly, simplified gyration, and atrophy
EEG to characterise the epileptic encephalopathy
Molecular analysis of the ASNS gene (the definitive test)
Metabolic screen to exclude other treatable encephalopathies
Genetic counselling given autosomal recessive recurrence risk
redFlags: Progressive microcephaly with refractory neonatal or infantile seizures
Severe startle, spasticity, or encephalopathy from birth
Rapid neurological deterioration and early mortality
Recurrence risk in future pregnancies requiring counselling
reference.prognosis: The prognosis is generally poor, with severe neurodevelopmental impairment, intractable epilepsy, and frequent death in infancy or early childhood. No disease-modifying therapy is established, and management is supportive.
pitfalls: Expecting a marked plasma metabolite abnormality when the biochemical changes are subtle
Missing the diagnosis without molecular testing
Assuming dietary asparagine supplementation will correct the central deficiency
Not offering genetic counselling for an autosomal recessive disorder
references: Nyhan, Atlas of Inherited Metabolic Diseases
management: Antiepileptic therapy to control the intractable seizures of this epileptic encephalopathy, often requiring combination anticonvulsants
Supportive neurological care for spasticity and the exaggerated startle, with antispasticity agents and management of irritability
Nutritional support and airway protection, including safe feeding and gastrostomy where there is dysphagia or aspiration risk
Consideration of dietary asparagine supplementation, acknowledging uncertain benefit because blood-brain-barrier uptake is limited
Multidisciplinary developmental, respiratory and palliative input given the severe neurodevelopmental impairment and high early mortality
Genetic counselling and family screening for this autosomal recessive disorder, with prenatal or preimplantation testing offered
